'''Sebastiaan Johan Edixhoven''' (12 March 1962<ref name="Leiden-obit"/><ref name="CV"/> – 16 January 2022<ref name="Leiden-obit"/><ref name="CIMPA-obit">{{cite web |url=https://www.cimpa.info/en/node/7180 |title=In Memoriam: The Passing of Bas Edixhoven |access-date=5 February 2022 |website=[[Centre International de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées]]}}</ref>) was a Dutch mathematician who worked in [[arithmetic geometry]]. He was a professor at [[University of Rennes 1]] and [[Leiden University]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-19 |title=In Memoriam - Bas Edixhoven |url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/news/2022/01/in-memoriam-bas-edixhoven |access-date=2024-10-11 |website=Leiden University |language=en}}</ref>

==Education==
Bas Edixhoven was born on 12 March 1962 in [[Leiden]], Netherlands.<ref name="thesis"/> Edixhoven graduated from {{ill|Erasmus College|nl|Erasmus College (Zoetermeer)}} in [[Zoetermeer]] in 1980.<ref name="thesis">{{cite thesis |url=https://websites.math.leidenuniv.nl/edixhoven/publications/1989/phd-thesis.pdf |title=Stable Models of Modular Curves and Applications |year=1989 |type=PhD |first=Bas |last=Edixhoven |publisher=[[Utrecht University]] }}</ref> He then studied at [[Utrecht University]] where he graduated with a master's degree in pure mathematics ''[[Latin honors#Netherlands|cum laude]]'' in 1985 and a PhD in mathematics in 1989, both under the direction of [[Frans Oort]].<ref name="CV"/><ref name="thesis"/><ref name="Mathematics">{{MathGenealogy|id=49938|name=Sebastiaan Johan Edixhoven}}</ref> His thesis was about [[modular curve]]s.<ref name="Leiden-obit"/>

==Career==
Edixhoven was a Morrey assistant professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1989 to 1991, after which he returned to Utrecht University.<ref name="Leiden-obit"/> From 1992 to 2002, he was a professor at the [[University of Rennes 1]].<ref name="Leiden-obit"/> He moved to [[Leiden University]] as a professor of geometry in 2002.<ref name="Leiden-obit"/>

In 2004, Edixhoven and [[Peter Stevenhagen]] established Leiden's participation in the Algebra, Geometry and Number Theory (ALGANT) collaborative program for master's and PhD students across French, Italian, German, Canadian, and Dutch universities.<ref name="Leiden-obit"/>

Edixhoven was a co-managing editor of ''[[Compositio Mathematica]]'' from 2003 to 2012.<ref name="Leiden-obit"/> He was an editor for ''Compositio Mathematica'' from 2000 to 2012,<ref name="Leiden-obit"/> for the ''[[Journal de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux]]'' from 1998 to 2004, for the ''[[Journal of Number Theory]]'' from 2004 to 2012, for ''[[Expositiones Mathematicae]]'' from 2003 to 2022, and for ''[[Indagationes Mathematicae]]'' from 2010 to 2022.<ref name="CV"/>

Edixhoven was involved in the Bèta-lerarenkamer think tank, which produced a mobile app for refugee teachers to improve their Dutch and mathematics abilities.<ref name="Leiden-obit"/>

==Research==
Edixhoven's early work was on modular curves.<ref name="Leiden-obit"/> He worked on the techniques used in [[Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem]] and the proof of [[Serre's modularity conjecture]].<ref name="Leiden-obit"/>

He later made important contributions regarding the [[André–Oort conjecture]], as well as making [[modular forms]] and associated [[Galois representations]] more computationally accessible.<ref name="Leiden-obit"/> His latest works had focused on geometric interpretations of the quadratic [[Chabauty method]].<ref name="Leiden-obit"/>

Outside of academia, he worked on [[Error detection and correction|correction codes]] for the [[Ministry of Armed Forces (France)|French Ministry of Defense]] and [[Canon Inc.]]<ref name="CV">{{cite web |url=http://www.math.leidenuniv.nl/~edix/cv.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae |access-date=5 February 2022 |archive-date=23 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220123005952/https://www.math.leidenuniv.nl/~edix/cv.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Awards==
From 1989 to 1992, Edixhoven was a recipient of the Huygens scholarship. From 1995 to 2002, he was a member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]]. In 2009, he became a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="Leiden-obit"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/6203 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121155333/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/6203 |title=Bas Edixhoven |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=21 January 2021}}</ref> In 2008, he gave an invited lecture at the 5th [[European Congress of Mathematics]].<ref name="CV"/>

==Death==
Edixhoven died on 16 January 2022, at the age of 59, from a [[tumor]].<ref name="Leiden-obit">{{cite news |last= |first= |date=19 January 2022|title=In Memoriam - Bas Edixhoven|trans-title= |url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/nieuws/2022/01/in-memoriam---bas-edixhoven|language=Dutch|work=[[Leiden University]]|location= |access-date=25 January 2022}}</ref><ref name="CIMPA-obit"/>
